# Common Parcel

> HOA management software for self-managed homeowners associations. It reads an
> association's own governing documents and then runs the dues, notices,
> violations, elections and vendor contracts on the schedule those documents and
> the relevant state statute already set. From $10 a month. Built in Detroit,
> Michigan; available anywhere in the United States.

Common Parcel is built for volunteer boards that run the association themselves,
without a property management company, a bookkeeper, or a designated software
person. It serves homeowners associations, condominium associations, planned
communities, and civic or neighbourhood associations of five to a thousand-plus
doors.

Contact: jesse@commonparcel.com — the founder answers.
Site: https://commonparcel.com/

## What it does

A board uploads its declaration, bylaws, rules and owner roster. Common Parcel
reads those documents and extracts the numbers that govern everything else — the
assessment amount, the due date, the grace period, the late fee, the meeting and
voting rules — and shows each one with the page and line it came from. Setup
usually takes about thirty minutes.

From then on it runs the association's recurring work automatically:

- Invoices dues and collects them by autopay, ACH or card
- Posts receipts to owner ledgers and reconciles the bank
- Applies late fees and issues the delinquency ladder of reminder, demand and lien
- Logs violations with photo and citation, and runs cure windows and re-inspections
- Carries architectural review requests on their statutory response clock
- Tracks vendor contracts and re-bids them before they renew
- Runs elections with electronic ballots and proxies, and tracks quorum
- Sends meeting notices and drafts minutes
- Writes every action to a numbered audit trail

## What the board still does

Anything with legal or financial weight stops for a person. A lien, a fine, or a
statutory notice requires two officers to sign; there is no batch approval and no
way for the software to sign on the board's behalf. A typical month leaves the
board two decisions and about twenty-two minutes of work.

## Custody of funds

Owners pay into the association's own bank account, in the association's own
name. Common Parcel is not in that payment path and has no ability to move
association money.

## Citations

Every notice quotes the provision, page and line it came from. If Common Parcel
cannot locate the governing provision, it prints a dash and says so rather than
inventing a citation.

## Pricing

Graduated per lot, per month, like a tax bracket: $2.50 each for the first 10
lots, $1.10 for lots 11 to 70, $0.40 for lots 71 to 500, and $0.50 above 500,
with a $10 monthly minimum.

- A four-lot association pays $10 a month
- A 100-lot association pays about $110 a month
- A 1,000-lot association pays about $513 a month

Everything is included — collections, violations, elections, vendor management,
documents and the audit trail — with no feature tiers and no per-notice charge.
Owners pay no fee to pay their dues. Civic and neighbourhood associations pay a
reduced rate. Billing is month to month with no contract, no setup fee, and a
full export of ledgers, documents, minutes and audit trail available in any
month, including the month an association leaves.

## Comparison

A local property management company typically charges $15 to $25 per door per
month, which is roughly $1,800 a month for a 100-home association. Other HOA
software platforms typically tier to $1.50 to $2.00 per door and still expect a
volunteer to configure the rules, remember the deadlines and write the notices.
Common Parcel configures itself from the association's own documents and runs the
month unattended.

## Migration

Common Parcel prepares the termination notice an existing management contract
requires, the records request, and a thirty-day transition checklist, then loads
the ledgers, documents and roster the association receives. There is no charge
for migration.

## Status

Common Parcel is onboarding founding associations now.
